content_metadata.description: Laura Chuhan Campbell discusses her candidacy for the UCU national executive committee, highlighting her motivations, the union's role, and the issues within universities.

qAndA.answer: She is running for UCU's national executive committee.
qAndA.question: What position is Laura Chuhan Campbell running for?

qAndA.answer: Laura mentions her eight years on precarious contracts, demonstrating the crucial support the union provided during a vulnerable period in her career. This adds weight to her argument that the union is essential for all members, regardless of their employment status.
qAndA.question: How does Laura's personal experience contribute to her message?

qAndA.answer: She mentions excessive workload, casualization, and management bullying.
qAndA.question: What specific issues within universities does Laura highlight?

qAndA.answer: She accuses universities of cynically using EDI agendas to justify authoritarian management practices that ultimately fail to benefit those with protected characteristics.
qAndA.question: How does Laura criticize the university system's approach to equality, diversity, and inclusion?

qAndA.answer: The video begins with a hopeful and grateful tone as Laura expresses her love for the union, transitions to a more critical and even angry mood as she exposes the injustices within the university system, and ends on a call to action, urging viewers to support a union that truly represents everyone.

text_to_speech: hello my name is laura chuhan campbell and i'm an assistant professor in the school of modern languages and cultures at durham university i'm standing for ucu's national executive committee for the first time not because i think ucu is broken and needs fixing but because i love this union yes it's got problems it's got its divisions but overall this is a union that really fights for its members i don't only see this on a national level with the uss dispute and the four fights but on a daily basis as a caseworker and branch organizer people in universities like to think of their workplace as an enlightened space which somehow transcends the prejudices and inequalities of the rest of the world of work in my work as a caseworker and an activist i am regularly confronted with evidence that this is not the case the university is not a welcoming and accessible space for people of color for trans people for young women for people with caring responsibilities people with disabilities people with intersections of those various characteristics all of whom are at the sharp end of problems that affect everyone in the university excessive workload casualization management bullying i see universities cynically using edi agendas to justify authoritarian management oversight in ways that don't actually better benefit anyone with protected characteristics and this is where ucu comes in shouldn't have to of course but as caseworkers departmental reps and committee members we're here to fight for all of our colleagues and they're here to fight for us there's no difference between the union and the members we are the union every single one of us from the rank and file member to the general secretary and that's why i'm putting myself forward to serve on the national executive committee i owe ucu a great deal it's given me space to find solidarity and community across the sector and it allows me to know that someone has got my back which was a huge comfort during the eight years on which i was on precarious contracts so that's why i'm standing i want to give some it back to the union and i want to be part of its overall direction i'm part of the ucu common slate that new awoke faction that everyone's talking about because i believe that the union isn't just for every single one of us it is every single one of us no matter your age race sexuality or gender identity or contract type thank you for listening

youtube_description:
Dr Laura Chuhan Campbell (Durham University) is running in the UCU NEC elections 2022, on the UCU Commons slate. She is a candidate for the North East HE seat, and for Representative of Women Members (HE) seat.

You could read her election statement here: https://www.ucu.org.uk/article/12052/Laura-Chuhan-Campbell-Durham-University

To find out more about UCU NEC elections 2022: https://www.ucu.org.uk/article/11791/UCU-trustee-officer-and-NEC-elections-in-2021-22

More on the UCU Commons slate: https://ucucommons.org/2021/01/11/ucu-nec-elections-2021-22/
